items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: Oh, Frankie Petit. Yeah, Frankie was here.

ctx.x: He was here then. You weren't here though when Buddy Petit and Frankie Dusen came out, were you?

Oh, Frankie Petit. Yeah, Frankie was here. I come in here. I come in here. It wasn't long. I come right in here when it is. There wasn't over... I was here for a couple of weeks. I used to go see Freddie was over at the Red Onion, Buddy Petit was playing over there. And Frankie was... Ding Johnson. See, Ding Johnson sent from. It was playing. That was right there at 10th and Central.
The Red Onion was 10th and Central. Yeah.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: I used to play pinch hit for Danny Lewis. Mm-hmm. With Frankie Deuce's band, you know.

ctx.x: That's really what they called me, Kid Galvin. Around there. Mm-hmm. I used to play pinch hit for Danny Lewis. Mm-hmm. With Frankie Deuce's band, you know.

items.q: Because all those bandleaders, they all liked me. There was something about it, I was friendly with all of them.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: He was playing with Frankie Dukeson.

ctx.x: Do you remember Danny Lewis? Danny Lewis?

I remember him well, that's my buddy. I used to pitch hit for him with the eagle. Yeah. He hit there, and Danny Lewis hit John and the Dots of the Island. We'd draw the pitch in there and say, we used to do what I always say, you see. Yeah. And we used to get behind them, you know, when they'd run, and say, da da da da da. Yeah. You know? So, what's that? Old Frankie Dukeson died, and old Danny Lewis cried. And Edward Barton put it aside. He could print good, he could draw good. He'd draw the side, and put all…
He was playing with Frankie Dukeson.
